questions.text: How to Facilitate • Encourage students to observe their surroundings like seasonal changes, the arrival of birds or butterflies, flowers, or changes in weather.
• Ask simple critical thinking questions like, “Where did this come from?” or “Why do we all use it?” to spark curiosity.
4. Think and write about the changes that you have noticed in yourself and your friends, in your school, and in your environment. Rhythms of Nature 9 Reprint 2026-27

1. Can you think of something that takes a really long time to change, maybe over years? India celebrates over 1,000 festivals throughout the year, making it one of the most festive countries. Changes are happening to us and to the world around us all the time. Some changes take years, some happen in just days or minutes! Have you noticed how things keep changing around you? Think about it. You grow taller each year, leaves fall off trees and grow again, flowers bloom, dry up and bloom again, the sky changes colour, the sun appears to rise and set every day. 4. Can you name something that changes in just a few minutes or even seconds? Changes Around Us in a Day (Day and Night) Just like we grow and change, the world around us is changing too. The day changes into night and the night becomes day. What causes day and night? The Sun seems to be rising in the east moving across the sky and setting in the west. So, is the Sun moving? Dong in Arunachal Pradesh is known as India’s ‘First Village of the Sunrise’. It is the very first place where the sun’s rays touch Indian land each morning. Reprint 2026-27
